speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis with possible underlying inflammatory arthritis (Rheumatoid Arthritis).

The history of pain at the thumb base worsened by lifting an infant, combined with radiation to the elbow and a family history of autoimmune disease, strongly suggests De Quervain's tenosynovitis potentially exacerbated by an underlying inflammatory condition. The normal measurements do not rule out this diagnosis, as functional limitations and specific tenderness are key clinical findings.
